note:
PMIDs that must never be indexed as corpus papers. Two DISTINCT disqualifiers live here and they must not be confused, because the remedy differs:
(1) PROVENANCE - the PMID resolves to a real record, which is precisely why every existence-checking gate passed it, but nothing in this repo ever cited it as evidence for a claim. It arrived from a code comment, a regex example or a bulk harvest. The right remedy is deletion; there was never anything there.
(2) RETRACTED (added 2026-08-26) - the paper WAS legitimately cited as evidence and the literature has since withdrawn it. Its provenance is sound; its findings are not. The right remedy is exclusion from the evidence base WITH the retraction recorded, so the repo can say why the evidence count changed and cannot silently re-ingest it. Retracted entries are found by audit_retractions.py, which reads PubMed's publication type - the one defect class where title agreement, topic screening and PMID resolution are all silent by construction, because a retracted paper passes every one of them.
This registry is PERSISTENT so that a later harvest cannot reintroduce an entry that a previous run adjudicated.

38918878.actual_title: Emerging insights into the role of IL-1 inhibitors and colchicine for inflammation management in type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
38918878.why: PubMed publication type is "Retracted Publication". Found 2026-08-26 by audit_retractions.py (new that day) while vetting the 37 papers folded in on 2026-08-25. Unlike every other entry in this registry its provenance was legitimate: it was cited in 18 files and published on three dashboards (Extracted_Evidence.html, Paper_Library.html, PMID_Verification.html), and it contributed 2 colchicine dose_response extractions to Gap 4 and Gap 7. It passed every existing gate - it resolves, it is on-topic, and its title is correct - because none of them asks about retraction. NOTE the stored title also drifted: the repo said "inflammation control", PubMed says "inflammation management".
38918878.evidence_removed: 2 dose_response extractions (colchicine 1.0 mg, 0.5 mg three times daily) mapped to Gap 4 and Gap 7
38918878.replacement_needed: The colchicine dosing claim is not necessarily wrong, but it can no longer rest on this paper. PMID 41889274 (Diab Vasc Dis Res 2026, systematic review/meta-analysis of colchicine for secondary cardiovascular prevention in diabetes) is already in the corpus and is a candidate replacement - it must be read before being used, not assumed.
